column1: # bq-schema.tsv (harbor#1278) — every table and field harbor's logs may hold in BigQuery, as data.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. Release 2 sends structured rows only: a closed schema, enum or numeric fields, no free text (#1278, "Log scope").
# So a fact table has no STRING column at all: every enum is an INT64 code into dim_enum, every time truncated. Free text then has no
# column to land in, even past the validator. bin/bq-format.sh judges rows against this file, and the BigQuery table schemas are
# generated from it (bq-format.sh bqschema), so the warehouse and the validator can't disagree.
# IDENTITY (#1278 "Log scope", amended again 2026-11-09: level 2). The one per-person field is person_id, a random id made once per
#   laptop account at install (or per Mac), never derived from a login or e-mail and never rotated. BigQuery holds no login, no HMAC
#   and no mapping: nothing here leads back to a person, and the loader drops the GitHub author before staging.
# GRAIN (D4, legal/dpia.md R3): a row that carries person_id is a day, never an hour or a minute. Finer times exist only in an
#   agg_ table, which carries no id and counts the people behind each cell. Anything shared beyond the operator is an anonymous
#   total with groups under 5 suppressed (templates/bq/views.sql, the v_shared_ views).
#   A per-person row is replaced whole for its (source, person, day) on every load, so a replay never adds and no comment id is kept.
# COLUMNS  table <TAB> field <TAB> type <TAB> set <TAB> nullable <TAB> source <TAB> question
#   type   code (INT64, a value of `set`) | codes (ARRAY<INT64>) | int, float (`set` is the range a..b) | bool | hour, minute
#          (TIMESTAMP with the lower parts zero; never beside person_id) | day (DATE) | rid (BYTES 16, the random id) | hex6, hex8
#          (BYTES 6 or 8: a core commit, a floor hash) | label (STRING: only in a dim_ table, only from this repo or the signed
#          policy). Nothing else: `bq-format.sh schema` refuses any other type, so a `string` row is red.
#   set    a set of contracts/bq-values.tsv; `a|b` accepts either. rule and check also take hub:<serial>:<index>, pack takes
#          hubpack:<index> (D6): the admin's names stay on the board
#   source where the value comes from on the laptop (member), the board, the loader or the Mac (operator)
